acq_cards.title: Treaty of Paris
acq_cards.text: Britain recognised the independence of the United States in the Treaty of Paris, which ended the Revolutionary War. The new country reached from the Atlantic to the Mississippi, and from the Great Lakes to Spanish Florida.
acq_cards.source: Wikipedia, 'Treaty of Paris (1783)'; Newberry Library AHCB

acq_cards.title: The Louisiana Purchase
acq_cards.text: The United States bought Louisiana from France for $15 million, about 828,000 square miles (2.1 million km²). It nearly doubled the country. Its western limits were not clearly defined; France formally handed it over on 20 December 1803.

acq_cards.title: West Florida
acq_cards.text: The United States claimed the Gulf coast between the Mississippi and the Perdido rivers as part of Louisiana; Spain disagreed. US forces took possession of the part west of the Pearl River on 10 December 1810, and the rest was added to Mississippi Territory in 1812.
acq_cards.source: Wikipedia, 'Territorial evolution of the United States'; Newberry Library AHCB

acq_cards.title: The 49th parallel
acq_cards.text: The Treaty of 1818 with Britain fixed the border along the 49th parallel from the Lake of the Woods to the Rocky Mountains. The Red River basin south of the line became American.

acq_cards.title: Florida from Spain
acq_cards.text: In the Adams-Onís Treaty, signed on 22 February 1819, Spain ceded Florida and the two countries drew their first boundary across the continent to the Pacific. It took effect in 1821.

acq_cards.title: Texas joins
acq_cards.text: Texas had declared independence from Mexico in 1836. The United States annexed it by a joint resolution of Congress, and Texas became a state on 29 December 1845. Mexico had not recognised the loss, and war followed in 1846.

acq_cards.title: The Oregon Treaty
acq_cards.text: Britain and the United States had shared the Oregon Country since 1818. The Oregon Treaty of 15 June 1846 split it along the 49th parallel.

acq_cards.title: The Mexican Cession
acq_cards.text: The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, signed on 2 February 1848, ended the Mexican-American War. Mexico ceded about 529,000 square miles (1.4 million km²), today's California, Nevada and Utah and parts of four more states. The United States paid $15 million and took over $3.25 million of Mexican debts to American citizens.
acq_cards.source: Wikipedia, 'Mexican Cession' and 'Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo'; Newberry Library AHCB

acq_cards.title: The Gadsden Purchase
acq_cards.text: For $10 million the United States bought 29,640 square miles (77,000 km²) of southern Arizona and New Mexico, land suited to a southern railroad to the Pacific. It set today's border with Mexico.

acq_cards.title: Alaska from Russia
acq_cards.text: Russia sold Alaska to the United States for $7.2 million, adding 586,412 square miles (1.5 million km²), about two cents an acre.

acq_cards.title: Hawaii annexed
acq_cards.text: Five years after Queen Liliʻuokalani was overthrown, Congress annexed Hawaii by joint resolution, signed by President McKinley on 7 July 1898. The queen protested that her throne had been taken illegally.

union_cards.title: South Carolina secedes
union_cards.text: Six weeks after Abraham Lincoln won the presidential election, a convention in South Carolina voted to leave the Union. Six more states of the Deep South followed by 1 February 1861.

union_cards.title: The Confederacy is formed
union_cards.text: Delegates of the seven seceded states formed the Confederate States of America at Montgomery, Alabama. Historians widely agree that preserving slavery was its principal aim.

union_cards.title: Fort Sumter
union_cards.text: Confederate forces fired on the federal fort in Charleston harbour, and the war began. Virginia, Arkansas, North Carolina and Tennessee seceded in the following eight weeks.

union_cards.title: Emancipation Proclamation
union_cards.text: Lincoln declared enslaved people in the areas still in rebellion to be free. It did not cover the slave states that had stayed in the Union.

union_cards.title: West Virginia
union_cards.text: The north-western counties of Virginia, which had rejected secession, were admitted as the new state of West Virginia.
union_cards.source: Newberry Library AHCB; Wikipedia, 'Confederate States of America'

union_cards.title: Gettysburg and Vicksburg
union_cards.text: In the first days of July 1863 the Union army turned back Lee's invasion of the North at Gettysburg, and Vicksburg on the Mississippi surrendered on 4 July.
union_cards.source: Wikipedia, 'Battle of Gettysburg' and 'Siege of Vicksburg'

union_cards.title: Surrender at Appomattox
union_cards.text: General Robert E. Lee surrendered his army at Appomattox Court House. Most other Confederate forces surrendered by May 1865.

union_cards.title: Slavery abolished
union_cards.text: The Thirteenth Amendment to the Constitution, abolishing slavery everywhere in the United States, was ratified.

union_cards.title: Georgia readmitted
union_cards.text: Georgia was the last former Confederate state readmitted; its representatives took their seats in Congress in February 1871.
union_cards.source: Wikipedia, 'Confederate States of America' and 'Reconstruction era'

cession_cards.title: Treaty of Greenville
cession_cards.text: After their defeat at Fallen Timbers in 1794, the nations of the Northwest Territory ceded most of what became Ohio. The treaty ended the Northwest Indian War.
cession_cards.source: Wikipedia, 'Treaty of Greenville'; USFS Royce cessions

cession_cards.title: Indian Removal Act
cession_cards.text: Congress authorised the President to exchange land west of the Mississippi for the homelands of nations in the East. About 60,000 Cherokee, Muscogee (Creek), Seminole, Chickasaw and Choctaw people were forced west in the years that followed.
cession_cards.source: Wikipedia, 'Indian Removal Act' and 'Trail of Tears'

cession_cards.title: Treaty of New Echota
cession_cards.text: A small Cherokee group signed away the nation's land in the Southeast. The Cherokee National Council never approved it and Principal Chief John Ross did not sign, but the Senate ratified it in 1836.

cession_cards.title: The Trail of Tears
cession_cards.text: The army began forcibly removing the Cherokee in May 1838. About 4,000 died on the way to Indian Territory, the figure the Cherokee Nation gives; other estimates run to 5,000.
cession_cards.source: Wikipedia, 'Trail of Tears' (Cherokee Nation; Oxford Research Encyclopedia of American History)

cession_cards.title: End of treaty-making
cession_cards.text: The Indian Appropriations Act of 1871 ended treaty-making: from then on, land was taken by acts of Congress and executive orders rather than by treaty.

cession_cards.title: The Dawes Act
cession_cards.text: The General Allotment Act split reservations into private plots and sold the 'surplus'. Land held by Native Americans fell from about 138 million acres in 1887 to 48 million in 1934.
